{"id": "4:6/q24", "question": "What does bidāran an yakbarū mean?", "turns_on": "Whether haste is one-sided or a race with the ward's approaching adulthood.", "positions": [{"id": "4:6/q24/p1", "position": "The guardian hastens to consume before the orphan grows and claims the estate", "reasons": "IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · ابن عباس: The prohibition addresses guardians: Ibn ʿAbbas says not to consume an orphan’s property without right, or hasten to consume it before the child grows up. RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author: Guardians must not consume the property wastefully or hasten to spend it before the orphans grow up and reclaim it; the phrase describes their waste and haste. RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author: The preceding warning against consuming wealth hastily before the orphan grows up shows why suspicion of guardians is well-founded and strengthens the case for witnessing delivery. NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author: Do not consume the property wastefully or rush to spend it before the orphans grow up and reclaim it; the verbal nouns are circumstantial or purposive. ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · ابن عباس وغيره: They say rushing means the guardian hastens to exploit the ward's estate before the ward matures, claiming to act before the child can take it back. SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · ابن عباس: Ibn Abbas says guardians hurried to consume orphans’ wealth before the child grew up and took the property back. IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author: Guardians are forbidden to consume orphan property wastefully or hastily before the orphans reach adulthood, unless there is a necessary need. DURR-FULL, d. 911 · ابن عباس: Test orphans when they reach puberty; if their judgment and handling of property are sound, hand over their wealth, and do not consume it wastefully or hastily before they mature. DURR-FULL, d. 911 · سعيد بن جبير: Do not consume the property without right or hastily before the orphan reaches puberty, fearing he will reclaim it. BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author: Guardians who hurry to spend fear that the orphans will mature, reclaim the estate, and restrict their spending. ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author: Mubadara means haste: the guardian may rush to consume the property before the orphan grows, while the orphan may hasten to reclaim it; the word is linked to fullness. ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author: The warning against consuming orphan property wastefully and before they grow supports Abu Hanifa’s view that property should not be withheld once they have grown, with the special delay for an immature adult explained earlier. {"id": "4:6/q30", "question": "What may a poor guardian take as maʿrūf?", "turns_on": "Whether the permission is a loan, wages, produce, subsistence, or no use of the ward's funds.", "positions": [{"id": "4:6/q30/p1", "position": "A poor guardian may take a fair wage for necessary service", "reasons": "IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · ابن عباس: A third view lets the guardian take a customary wage for work done for the orphan, reported from Ibn ʿAbbas and ʿAʾisha. IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · الحسن: Some authorities say a guardian who later becomes solvent need not repay, since the amount is compensation for his service. RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author: One legal view allows a needy guardian to use from the ward’s wealth what is needed and a fair amount for the work; the verse’s contrast and its distinction between unjust and non-unjust consumption support this allowance. | mentions 4:10 RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · ابن عباس: Another report from Ibn ʿAbbās says the guardian may eat moderately by sharing in their work but should not wear even a turban beyond that allowance. RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author: Guardianship work may merit compensation by analogy with collectors of charity, who receive a designated share. QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · إبراهيم وعطاء والحسن البصري والنخعي وقتادة: A second view says a poor guardian owes no repayment because modest food and clothing are compensation from God for responsible care; luxury clothing is excluded, and the jurists support it by analogy to an imam's stipend. QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن عباس وأبو العالية والشعبي: Another explanation allows use of an orphan's livestock milk, servants, or animals so long as the estate is not harmed; jurists compare this to fair wages, with any excess forbidden. QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · أبو العباس: Abu al-Abbas allows fair compensation when a large estate demands substantial work; for a trivial estate he permits only customary small quantities of milk, food, or ghee without harm or excess. QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author: Al-Qurtubi says abstaining from compensation is better; he condemns fees taken by partition judges and their agents as unlawful and within the threat against consuming orphan property. | mentions 4:10 BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author: A wealthy guardian abstains; a poor guardian may take a customary amount proportionate to need and work, since the language implies a limited right in the child's property. ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · طائفة، الإمام أحمد: Some say reasonable means compensation proportionate to the guardian's service; one report attributes this to Ahmad. IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · عائشة: Aisha says the allowance concerns an orphan's guardian who manages and improves the estate and is needy; he may eat a customary amount proportionate to his work. IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author: Jurists cap a needy guardian's draw at the lesser of a fair wage for the work or the amount needed. IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · الشافعي: One view requires no repayment if the guardian later becomes solvent; al-Shafi'i's companions prefer it because the verse permits eating without requiring compensation. BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author: A wealthy guardian should abstain entirely from the orphan’s property; a poor guardian who manages it may take only customary compensation for his work. BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author: The poor guardian’s customary allowance is proportionate to the wage earned through his effort. BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author: A poor guardian may take a customary lawful amount for necessary needs and fair compensation for work, showing a trustee’s service-based right. ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · ابن عباس: A poor guardian may take from an orphan's assets in proportion to the work and benefit he provides, without extravagance or waste. ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author: Whether the guardian's permitted consumption counts as wages has two opinions; the author's school takes the second, as al-Jassas states in al-Ahkam.
